doc.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recording break and how his careers flow together
summary: After an interruption, Schwartz and Schuller marvel at how his careers connect.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Was I in the middle of something?

We were talking about Scott Joplin and Tremonisha and your arrangement of that. That leads me, if you want, into some of your experience – what I’m really hearing and loving, is how you said that some people concentrate on this thing and then they concentrate on that and then they concentrate on that, but with you, you’ve amalgamated all of these disciplines into who you are, and one thing just leads to another. We started talking about working in radio and all of a sudden we’re off into – it just seems to . . .
It just seems to all flow together.
Can you imagine how fascinating my life is? It’s unbelievable, how lucky I am.
Yeah. It’s truly an astounding life. Did you conduct the opera when it was first performed?
Was that not the first time you conducted an orchestra?
